newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iraqi opposition calls for Saddam's downfall.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi opposition calls for Saddam's downfall.

text.p: An Iraqi opposition group on Monday called for the downfall of President Saddam Hussein and said he should be tried for genocide.

"What happened in Kurdistan in the last few days is further proof that there will be no peace and no stability in Iraq and the region without the fall of Saddam and his dictatorial regime," said the Iraqi National Congress (INC) in a statement faxed to Reuters.
The umbrella opposition group said ending the current crisis in northern Iraq would require certain conditions such as the withdrawal of Iraqi forces from the Kurdish enclave in northern Iraq.
It also said the Iraqi president should be tried for war crimes, violations of human rights and genocide.

The KDP -- which had previously backed the INC -- on Monday captured the Kurdish stronghold of Sulaimaniya from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, United Nations guards and relief officials said.
The latest tensions in the region came after Iraqi forces intervened in the region last week to help the KDP capture the main Kurdish city of Arbil.
Baghdad, which actively backed the KDP assault on Arbil, has denied taking part in further operations.
The INC condemned the stand taken by KDP leaders for their alliance with Baghdad and called on the group to resume the fight against Saddam.
